name: commitwork
description: Repository security scanner, local CI runner and scheduled monitor, with remediation and compliance-evidence tooling. Manifest-driven; runs against any git repository.
filesNote: The publishable unit is the whole tracked tree except ci/ and CLAUDE.md (operator ruling D25, 2026-10-07). This list is the npm package's subset: the runtime directories, mcp/ (the MCP server, and mcp/tools.mjs, which the wire layer licenses under Apache-2.0), and the licence files the package's licence statements point to. LICENSE-APACHE-2.0 is listed because npm's automatic inclusion takes LICENSE but not a suffixed name, so the Apache carve-out shipped without its text; bin/test/npm-pack-contents.test.mjs holds the list to the wire-layer manifest. Without a files list npm packs the working tree minus ignore rules, which measured 2185 entries / 46.2 MB on 2026-10-05 and included CLAUDE.md, every private monitor record, the eight pre-lifecycle backups, ci/, prompts/, docsite/ and an untracked sleight_data/posture.db — npm pack reads the WORKING TREE, so an untracked local file ships while a gitignored one does not. LICENSING.md is listed because `license` says SEE LICENSE IN LICENSING.md and npm's automatic inclusions cover LICENSE/LICENCE, not this filename, so omitting it leaves the licence field pointing at nothing. The negations are belt-and-braces over the private records rather than the mechanism that protects them: the mechanism is that those paths leave the repository. A negation keeps them out of the tarball even on a tree where the move has not landed, and costs nothing once it has.
